nodes.content: Develop a learned large-eddy closure reconciling local energy backscatter with long-horizon stability across unseen Reynolds numbers.
requirements: Reduce kinetic-energy spectrum error by 20% versus dynamic Smagorinsky on held-out Reynolds numbers.
Maintain bounded kinetic energy for 100 eddy-turnover times without suppressing all local backscatter.

nodes.content: Train a Galilean-invariant stress network with spectral loss and an energy-dependent global injection cap that preserves local backscatter.
Should the injection cap limit instantaneous domain-wide subgrid transfer or its running mean to preserve intermittent backscatter?
Unlike a ten-turnover running-mean cap, instantaneous global capping will bound energy for 100 turnovers while preserving ≥10% backscattering cells.
Train identical closures with instantaneous versus ten-turnover running-mean caps; compare 100-turnover energy bounds, backscatter fractions, and held-out-Re spectral errors.
Run 100-turnover LES at held-out Reλ=180,300; compare instantaneous and running-mean caps on energy bounds, backscatter fractions, and spectral errors.
At held-out Reλ=180/300, instantaneous caps kept energy below 1.4K_DNS for 100 turnovers with 13% backscattering cells; running-mean caps exceeded 2K_DNS.
Adopt instantaneous global injection capping: it bounded 100-turnover energy while retaining 13% backscattering cells, unlike running-mean capping.
Benchmark the instantaneous-capped closure against dynamic Smagorinsky at held-out Reλ=180/300 using spectrum error and 100-turnover energy trajectories.
LES-Bench v1 report containing Reλ=180/300 spectral-error comparisons against dynamic Smagorinsky, 100-turnover energy trajectories, and local backscatter fractions.
Compare instantaneous and running-mean caps on held-out Reλ=180/300 LES using wavenumber-resolved spectral error and subgrid-transfer PDFs.
Held-out Reλ=180/300 relative spectrum L1 errors: instantaneous 0.23, running-mean 0.21, dynamic Smagorinsky 0.25; stable cap improves only 8%.
Audit instantaneous-cap interventions by correlating shellwise spectral residuals with cap activation and clipped subgrid injection at Reλ=180/300.
Cap triggered on 4% of steps; clipped injection tracked high-k deficits (r=0.61), while 13% of cells backscattered.
Can wavenumber-selective injection capping reduce high-k spectral deficits while maintaining bounded energy for 100 turnovers?
Reallocate injection from low-k to high-k shells under the same instantaneous energy budget; test held-out spectra and 100-turnover stability.
Implement budget-preserving shellwise injection reallocation prioritizing k>0.6k_c; compare 100-turnover Reλ=180/300 spectra, energy, and backscatter against the original cap.
ShellCap-v2 module and benchmark bundle containing budget-preserving high-k reallocation, Reλ=180/300 spectra, energy trajectories, and backscatter logs.
Train a scale-conditioned residual-stress network with spectral loss and energy-triggered eddy viscosity that retains negative local subgrid transfer.
At what kinetic-energy threshold should eddy viscosity activate to arrest growth without erasing local backscatter at Reλ=300?
At Reλ=300, activating viscosity above 1.2K_ref (five-turnover baseline) will keep energy below 1.4K_ref for 100 turnovers, retaining ≥10% backscattering cells.
Run 100-turnover Reλ=300 LES with activation thresholds 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3K_ref; record peak energy and backscattering-cell fraction.
At Reλ=300, the 1.2K_ref trigger peaked at 1.56K_ref over 100 turnovers, despite 12% backscattering cells.
Augment nonnegative dynamic Smagorinsky with a learned, Reynolds-normalized zero-net-work stress that redistributes shellwise energy and permits local backscatter.
Train the zero-net-work residual on Reλ=100/140/220; test LES-Bench v1 Reλ=180/300 spectral L1, 100-turnover energy, and backscatter against dynamic Smagorinsky.
At Reλ=180/300, spectral L1 was 0.19 versus Smagorinsky’s 0.25; peak energy stayed ≤1.4K_ref over 100 turnovers, with 12% backscattering cells.
Audit residual net work, spectral L1, and peak energy across five seeds and 64³/128³ grids at Reλ=180/300.
At 128³, five-seed Reλ=300 spectral L1 was 0.24 versus Smagorinsky’s 0.25, missing the 20% target.
Can k/k_c conditioning restore the zero-net-work closure’s ≥20% spectral-L1 improvement at 128³, Reλ=300 without destabilizing energy?
k/k_c-conditioned zero-net-work stress will achieve 128³ Reλ=300 spectral L1 ≤0.20, 100-turnover energy ≤1.4K_ref, and ≥10% backscattering cells.
Condition residual stress on k/k_c, enforce zero net work, then compare five-seed 128³ Reλ=300 spectral error, energy, and backscatter.
Run five-seed, 100-turnover 128³ Reλ=300 LES; compare conditioned stress with unconditioned stress and Smagorinsky on spectral L1, energy, and backscatter.
Five-seed 128³ Reλ=300: spectral L1 0.19 versus 0.24 unconditioned and 0.25 Smagorinsky; 100-turnover peak energy ≤1.35K_ref; backscatter 11%.
Ablate k/k_c conditioning across five fresh 128³ Reλ=300 seeds; measure spectral L1, 100-turnover peak energy, and backscatter.
Across five fresh 128³ Reλ=300 seeds, conditioned spectral L1 averaged 0.22 versus Smagorinsky’s 0.25, missing the ≤0.20 prediction.
Do fresh-seed spectral failures stem from high-k transfer miscalibration or seed-dependent forcing statistics at 128³ Reλ=300?
Fresh-seed failures reflect underpredicted high-k backscatter, not forcing variation; shellwise calibration is needed to reach spectral L1 ≤0.20.
Compare shellwise transfer and forcing statistics between original and fresh 128³ seeds; calibrate high-k stress if transfer bias persists.
At 128³ Reλ=300, compute seedwise high-k subgrid transfer bias and forcing-power variance for original versus fresh five-seed cohorts.
Fresh seeds underpredicted filtered-DNS high-k backscatter by 18% versus 4% originally; forcing-power CV was 3% in both cohorts.
Retain k/k_c conditioning, add high-k transfer calibration, and require fresh-seed validation: spectral L1 rose 0.19→0.22 alongside an 18% backscatter deficit.
Calibrate high-k transfer on training Reynolds numbers; rerun matched-forcing fresh-seed 128³ Reλ=300 LES, measuring spectral L1 and energy.
HighK-Cal v1 checkpoint and matched-forcing 128³ Reλ=300 benchmark bundle with shellwise transfer, spectral L1, and 100-turnover energy traces.
Train a Reynolds-normalized stochastic stress model with a Lyapunov-constrained drift and shellwise spectral loss, retaining intermittent local backscatter.
How strongly can stochastic high-k stress fluctuate before its energy injection overwhelms the Lyapunov-constrained drift?
High-k noise capped at 10% of dissipative power bounds 100-turnover energy below 1.4K_ref while retaining ≥10% backscattering cells.
Sweep high-k noise caps of 5%, 10%, and 20% dissipative power in 100-turnover Reλ=180/300 LES; measure energy and backscatter.
At Reλ=180/300, the 10% cap kept 100-turnover peak energy ≤1.36K_ref and 12% backscattering cells; 20% reached 1.72K_ref.
Run fresh-seed 128³ Reλ=180/300 LES comparing 10%-noise stochastic closure with ShellCap-v2 benchmarks on spectral L1, 100-turnover energy, and backscatter.
Fresh-seed 128³ Reλ=300 spectral L1 was 0.23 versus ShellCap-v2’s 0.21 and Smagorinsky’s 0.25, missing the 20% target.
Ablate stochastic forcing in five-seed Reλ=180/300 LES; compare high-k spectral L1 and backscatter against the deterministic drift-only closure.
At Reλ=300, stochastic forcing reduced high-k spectral L1 from 0.27 to 0.23 and raised backscattering cells from 7% to 12%.
Can DNS-matched shellwise noise covariance lower fresh-seed Reλ=300 spectral L1 to ≤0.20 without exceeding the 10% injection cap?
Fit DNS covariance using ablation-isolated high-k gains; retest against fresh-seed L1=0.23, targeting ≤0.20 under 10% cap.
Fit shellwise covariance on training DNS; run five fresh-seed, 100-turnover 128³ Reλ=300 LES, tracking spectral L1, energy, and injection.
Fresh-seed Reλ=300 spectral L1 reached 0.19 versus Smagorinsky’s 0.25; energy ≤1.38K_ref over 100 turnovers, injection ≤10%, backscatter 12%.
Adopt DNS-covariance stochastic closure: noise ablation supports backscatter; fresh-seed L1 improved 0.23→0.19 with 100-turnover energy ≤1.38K_ref.
Run ten independent 128³ Reλ=300 DNS-covariance LES; verify spectral L1 ≤0.20, injection ≤10%, bounded 100-turnover energy, and backscatter.
CovLES-v1 validation bundle: ten-seed Reλ=300 spectral L1, injection-cap logs, backscatter fractions, and 100-turnover energy traces.
Train a scale-conditioned mixed-stress closure with a dissipation-funded reservoir enabling local backscatter, cumulative passivity, and shellwise spectral loss.
What reservoir capacity preserves high-k backscatter without exhausting dissipation credit during 100-turnover LES at held-out Reλ=300?
A reservoir capped at 0.15K_ref will sustain ≥10% backscattering cells while keeping peak energy ≤1.4K_ref over 100 turnovers.
Sweep reservoir capacities 0.05, 0.15, and 0.30K_ref across held-out Reλ=180/300 LES; track depletion, backscatter, energy, and spectra.
Run 100-turnover 128³ Reλ=300 reservoir sweeps (0.05/0.15/0.30K_ref); benchmark depletion, spectral L1, energy, and backscatter against HighK-Cal v1 and CovLES-v1.
At Reλ=300, the 0.15K_ref reservoir achieved spectral L1=0.18 versus Smagorinsky’s 0.25; 100-turnover peak energy was 1.34K_ref, backscatter 13%, depletion 2%.
Stress-test the 0.15K_ref reservoir across ten fresh Reλ=180/300 seeds; audit depletion, passivity, backscatter, spectral L1, and 100-turnover energy.
Fresh Reλ=180 seeds yielded spectral L1=0.22 versus Smagorinsky’s 0.25 (12% improvement), despite ≤1.38K_ref energy and 12% backscatter.
Does the Reλ=180 spectrum miss arise from reservoir depletion or Reynolds-dependent low-k stress bias?
At Reλ=180, replace 0.15K_ref with 0.05K_ref: low-k bias, not depletion, drives spectral error; expect ≥10% backscatter and ≤1.4K_ref energy.
Retain Reλ=300’s 0.15K_ref setting; compare 0.05/0.15K_ref on fresh Reλ=180 seeds for low-k bias, depletion, spectral L1, energy, and backscatter.
Run paired 100-turnover Reλ=180 LES at 0.05/0.15K_ref; compare low-k transfer bias, reservoir depletion, spectral L1, energy, and backscatter.
At Reλ=180, shrinking reservoir 0.15→0.05K_ref cut low-k bias 16%→5% and spectral L1 0.22→0.19; depletion 4%, backscatter 11%, peak energy 1.36K_ref.
Replay matched Reλ=180 filtered-DNS trajectories with 0.05/0.15K_ref reservoirs; measure low-k stress error conditional on credit depletion.
Matched Reλ=180 replay attributed 78% of 0.15K_ref low-k stress error to exhausted-credit frames; outside depletion, bias was 4%.
Why does the 0.15K_ref reservoir exhaust credit during low-k transfer events despite only 2% overall depletion at Reλ=300?
At Reλ=180, high-k withdrawal bursts precede low-k events and exhaust shared credit, causing depletion-linked stress error.
Align paired reservoir runs with depletion-labeled DNS replays; test whether high-k withdrawals precede low-k stress errors at Reλ=180.
Cross-correlate shellwise withdrawals with depleted-credit low-k stress errors across matched Reλ=180 trajectories, stratifying 0.05/0.15K_ref capacities.
At Reλ=180, high-k withdrawal bursts preceded 81% of depleted-credit low-k errors within 0.3 turnovers at 0.15K_ref capacity.
Retain the reservoir closure with scale-conditioned capacity and protected low-k credit: 0.05K_ref improved Reλ=180 spectra; high-k bursts depleted 0.15K_ref.
Implement protected low-k credit and scale-conditioned 0.05–0.15K_ref capacity; test fresh-seed Reλ=180/300 spectral L1, depletion, backscatter, and 100-turnover energy.
ReservoirLES-v2 checkpoint and fresh-seed Reλ=180/300 benchmark bundle with protected-credit logs, spectral L1, backscatter fractions, and 100-turnover energy traces.
